dictionary.definition: baby, child; children

etymology.hint: child

currentComponents.note: 子 (child) — 孩 relates directly to children
亥 (hài) gives a sound close to 孩's reading hái

dictionary.definition: son, child; seed, egg; fruit; small thing

etymology.hint: A child in a wrap, with outstretched arms but bundled legs

currentComponents.note: A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

dictionary.definition: to begin, to initiate; to rise, to stand up

etymology.hint: walk

currentComponents.note: 走 (to walk/run) — 起 relates to standing up and setting into motion.
己 (jǐ) gives a close sound cue — 起 is pronounced qǐ, sharing the same final sound.

dictionary.definition: to arrive, to come, to return; in the future, later on

etymology.hint: A wheat plant that has not yet borne fruit; compare 來

currentComponents.note: Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

dictionary.definition: place, location; "that which", a particle introducing a passive clause

etymology.hint: An axe 斤 swung at a door 户

currentComponents.note: 户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'

dictionary.definition: little, few; rather, somewhat

etymology.hint: two

currentComponents.note: 二 (two) — 些 originally suggested a small plural amount, building on the idea of 'more than one.'
此 (cǐ) is the historical phonetic element; it no longer closely matches the modern reading xiē.

dictionary.definition: also, besides; still, yet; to return

etymology.hint: Not 不 moving 辶

currentComponents.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — relates to motion or progress.
不 (not) — 'not yet moving on' gave 还 its meaning of 'still, yet.'

dictionary.definition: to ask about, to inquire after

etymology.hint: mouth

currentComponents.note: 口 (mouth) — 问 relates to speaking, specifically asking a question.
门 (mén) gives a hint of the sound — 问 is pronounced wèn, related but the tone and vowel have shifted.

dictionary.definition: forehead; headline, title; theme

etymology.hint: head

currentComponents.note: 页 (head/page) — 题 relates to the forehead or the topmost part, extending to the 'title' or 'topic' placed at the top.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 题 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.

dictionary.definition: to open; to start, to initiate, to begin

etymology.hint: Simplified form of 開; hands 廾 lifting the latch 一 of a door

currentComponents.note: 廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'

dictionary.definition: to begin, to start; beginning

etymology.hint: woman

currentComponents.note: 女 (woman) — 始's meaning 'beginning' has been linked to the idea of the origin of life.
台 (tái) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shǐ.

dictionary.definition: between, among; midpoint; space, place, locality

etymology.hint: The sun 日 shining through a doorway 门

currentComponents.note: 门 (door/gate) — 间 pictures light passing through an entryway.
日 (sun) — sunlight shining through a gap in a doorway gave 间 its meaning of a space 'in between,' as in 中间 (in the middle) or 时间 (time, the space between moments).

dictionary.definition: labor, work; laborer, worker

etymology.hint: A spade or other workman's tool

currentComponents.note: 工 depicts a carpenter's square or workman's tool — a simple shape that came to represent work and labor.

dictionary.definition: to make; to write, to compose; to act, to perform

etymology.hint: A person 亻 making something for the first time 乍; 乍 also provides the pronunciation

currentComponents.note: 亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

dictionary.definition: certainly; naturally; suddenly

etymology.hint: fire

currentComponents.note: 灬 (fire) — 然 originally described burning; the meaning later shifted to 'so, correct' as 然 became a grammatical particle.
肰 (rán) gives the sound — 然 is also pronounced rán, an exact match.

dictionary.definition: after; behind, rear; descendants

currentComponents.note: 后 originally pictured a ruler seated with mouth open, issuing a command, an image tied to authority. That is why it came to mean 'queen, empress' as well as, in its simplified role, 'after, behind.'

dictionary.definition: affair, matter, business; to serve; accident, incident

currentComponents.note: 事 originally pictured a hand holding a forked tally stick or ceremonial staff, used by officials to record duties. Over time the image was abstracted into a compact character meaning 'affair, matter, to serve.'

dictionary.definition: emotion, feeling, sentiment

etymology.hint: heart

currentComponents.note: 忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.

dictionary.definition: just, simply; to go to; to approach, near

etymology.hint: specialty

currentComponents.note: 尤 (particularly/outstanding) — relates to 就's sense of approaching or arriving at a particular point
京 (jīng, capital) gives a sound close to 就's pronunciation jiù

dictionary.definition: below, underneath; inferior; to bring down; next

etymology.hint: One stroke under another; compare 上 (above)

currentComponents.note: A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

dictionary.definition: not, negative, non-; to oppose

etymology.hint: Two bird's wings opposed; two people back-to-back

currentComponents.note: Depicts two things splayed apart from each other — such as a bird's two wings, or two people standing back-to-back — later used for the meaning 'not, contrary to.'

dictionary.definition: common, general, normal; always, frequently, regularly

etymology.hint: cloth

currentComponents.note: 巾 (cloth) — 常 originally referred to a long skirt or banner made of cloth, later coming to mean something 'usual' or 'ordinary.'
尚 (shàng) gives a hint of the sound — 常 is pronounced cháng, a connection that has drifted over time.

dictionary.definition: to look, to see; to examine, to scrutinize

etymology.hint: Shielding one's eyes 目 with a hand 手 to look to the distance

currentComponents.note: 手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'

dictionary.definition: to go to, to arrive

etymology.hint: arrive

currentComponents.note: 至 (zhì, to arrive) — carries 到's core meaning, 'to reach, to arrive'
刂 (a form of 刀, dāo) gives a sound close to 到's pronunciation dào

dictionary.definition: rare; to hope for, to strive for; to expect

currentComponents.note: 爻 (crossed, interwoven strands) — pictures a loosely woven pattern, the idea of something thin or sparse.
巾 (cloth) — a piece of loosely woven cloth gave 希 its early meaning 'sparse, rare,' which later extended figuratively to 'hope,' something rare and longed for.

dictionary.definition: to expect, to hope, to look forward to

etymology.hint: A king 王 gazing at the moon 月; 亡 provides the pronunciation

currentComponents.note: Depicts a person standing tall, gazing up at the moon 月 — the image of looking into the distance, the source of 望's meaning 'to gaze, hope, expect.'

dictionary.definition: appropriate, timely; to act, to serve; the sound of bells

currentComponents.note: 当 (simplified from 當) combined 田 (a field) with 尚, and originally referred to comparing two fields to judge whether their value was equal. That sense of correspondence broadened into 当's meanings 'to correspond to, to serve as, to be when.'

dictionary.definition: also, too

currentComponents.note: 也 is thought to have originally been a pictograph of a coiled snake, or possibly a ladle, though scholars disagree on the exact image. Whatever its original referent, the character was borrowed purely for its sound to serve as the grammatical particle meaning 'also, too,' the meaning it retains today.

dictionary.definition: to consent, to permit; to promise, to betroth

etymology.hint: speech

currentComponents.note: 讠 (speech) — 许 relates to giving permission through words.
午 (wǔ) gives a hint of the sound — 许 is pronounced xǔ, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

dictionary.definition: friend, pal, acquaintance

etymology.hint: Two people 月 walking together

currentComponents.note: 月, appearing twice side by side, originally depicted two people (or two strings of shells) together — giving 朋 its meaning 'friend, companion.'

dictionary.definition: friend, companion; fraternity

etymology.hint: Two hands 又 joined, representing friendship; 又 also provides the pronunciation

currentComponents.note: 又 (hand), shown twice and joined together — two hands clasped in friendship gave 友 its meaning 'friend.'

dictionary.definition: mother, mama

etymology.hint: woman

currentComponents.note: 女 (woman) — 妈 refers to one's mother
马 (mǎ) gives a sound close to 妈's reading mā, differing only in tone

dictionary.definition: mutual, reciprocal; equal; each other

etymology.hint: To stare 目 at a tree 木, meaning to observe

currentComponents.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'

dictionary.definition: to trust, to believe; letter, sign

currentComponents.note: 亻 (person) — the human party whose word is at stake.

言 (speech) — combined with 亻 (person), the image of a person standing behind their own words gave 信 its meanings 'to trust, to believe' and, by extension, 'a letter' — a trusted message carried between people.

dictionary.definition: to know, to recognize, to understand

etymology.hint: speech

currentComponents.note: 讠 (speech) — 认 relates to recognizing or acknowledging something, often expressed through words.
人 (rén) gives the sound — 认 is pronounced rèn, a close variant of the same sound.

dictionary.definition: son, child

etymology.hint: Simplified form of 兒, a picture of a child; compare 人

currentComponents.note: 儿 (simplified from 兒) depicts a small child, drawn with a large head on a small body — a simple picture of youth.

dictionary.definition: modern, current; today, now

etymology.hint: A mouth 亼 talking about things

currentComponents.note: 亼 — traditionally linked to an image of gathering or covering; its original pictorial sense has become obscure, but the character came to mean 'now, the present.'

dictionary.definition: sky, heaven; god, celestial

etymology.hint: The heavens 一 above a man 大

currentComponents.note: 大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'

dictionary.definition: bright, clear; to explain, to understand, to shed light

etymology.hint: The light of the sun 日 and moon 月

currentComponents.note: 日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.

dictionary.definition: white; clear, pure, unblemished; bright

etymology.hint: A burning candle; the rays of the sun

currentComponents.note: Originally depicted a burning candle or the sun's rays radiating outward — the source of 白's meaning 'white, bright, clear.'

dictionary.definition: straight, vertical; candid, direct, frank

etymology.hint: To look someone in the eye 目

usedInWords.meaning: direct (opposite: indirect 間接|间接[jian4 jie1])

currentComponents.note: 十 (here a straight vertical line) — 直 pictures something drawn perfectly straight.
目 (eye) — looking directly and steadily with the eye gave 直 its meaning 'straight' or 'direct.'

dictionary.definition: earth, ground, soil; land, region; structural particle used before a verb

etymology.hint: earth

currentComponents.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'

dictionary.definition: square, rectangle; side; region; flag

currentComponents.note: 方 is thought to have originally pictured a plow or a forked tool with square corners, later extended to describe squareness, direction, and by extension a proper method or way of doing something.

dictionary.definition: no, not, un-; negative prefix

etymology.hint: A bird flying toward the sky 一

currentComponents.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'

dictionary.definition: pass; to go across, to pass through

etymology.hint: walk

currentComponents.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過

dictionary.definition: to issue, to dispatch, to send out; hair

currentComponents.note: 发 is a simplified form of 發, whose ancient shape combined a bow with a hand pulling back to release an arrow. The image of a sudden release gave the character its core meaning 'to send out, to issue, to set off.'

dictionary.definition: to return, to turn around; a time

etymology.hint: Originally, a spiral signifying return

currentComponents.note: 回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'

dictionary.definition: standard, accurate; to permit, to approve, to allow

etymology.hint: water in a spirit level

currentComponents.note: 冫 (water) — 准 originally referred to a carpenter's level using water to check flatness, extended to 'standard, accurate, level.'
隹 (zhuī) gives a sound hint — 准 is pronounced zhǔn, sharing the base sound though the vowel and tone differ somewhat.

dictionary.definition: to prepare; to get ready, to equip; ready; perfect

etymology.hint: To go 夂 to the farm 田 to prepare for a harvest

currentComponents.note: 夂 (to go) — heading out.
田 (farm field) — going out to the fields ahead of the harvest season, the act of preparation giving 备 its meaning 'to prepare, get ready.'

dictionary.definition: to search for, to look for, to find; change (as in money)

etymology.hint: To go searching with a spear 戈 in hand 扌

currentComponents.note: 扌 (hand) — represents an action performed by hand.
戈 (a spear/dagger-axe) — an old image of searching or probing with a weapon in hand, giving 找 its meaning 'to search, to look for.'
